html:
Behzad was a Persian painter of book illustrations, the master of Persian miniature painting. He worked first at Herat and later at Tabriz.

At Herat he served the court of Husayn Bayqara, last great ruler of the Timurids, with support from the poet and minister Ali-Shir Nava'i. Earlier painting tended to show stiff, formal scenes. Behzad filled his pages with lively people doing ordinary things: builders on scaffolds, men at a bath house, dervishes dancing. His figures move and his colours are carefully balanced.

When the Safavids took Herat, Behzad moved west. Under Shah Ismail I he was made head of the royal library and workshop in Tabriz, where he trained the next generation of court painters. His style shaped Persian, Ottoman and Mughal painting for a century.
sum: Behzad was a Persian painter of book illustrations, the master of Persian miniature painting. He worked first at Herat and later at Tabriz.
